{{nihongo|'''Okada Kamo Shrine'''|岡田鴨神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

=== History ===
[[File:Okada-Kamo-jinja, torii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]
According to a fragment of the *Yamashiro no Kuni Fudoki*, Taketsunumi no Mikoto traveled from Katsuragi in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}, passed through Okada Kamo in Yamashiro Province, and came to rest at {{ill|Shimogamo Shrine|Q701620|qid=Q701620}} (Shimogamo Shrine) in northern Kyoto. It is said that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, the Kamo clan received a divided spirit from Shimogamo Shrine and founded this shrine at Okada Kamo, a place associated with Taketsunumi no Mikoto.

The earliest documentary reference appears in the *{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}*, in an entry dated the 27th day of the first month of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), which records that the shrine was granted the divine rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}).

In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed under {{ill|Yamashiro Province|Q749276|qid=Q749276}}, {{ill|Sōraku District, Kyoto|Q1154661|qid=Q1154661}} as “Okada Kamo Shrine, Major, Tsukinami and Niiname,” placing it among the Shikidai Taisha and noting that it received offerings at the court’s {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}.

The shrine was originally located north of its present site (on the bank of the {{ill|Kizu River|Q3746236|qid=Q3746236|lt=Kizugawa River}}, where the site known as “Kamo Daimyōjin Ruins” remains). However, repeated flooding caused by changes in the river’s course led to its relocation to the current location. The present site is said to be the former location of the Okada Detached Palace of {{ill|Empress Genmei|Q233224|qid=Q233224}}. After the palace fell into disuse, villagers established a shrine to preserve the former palace grounds, calling it “Tenjin Shrine.” Okada Kamo Shrine was later relocated into that precinct. Today, the Tenmangū stands as a subsidiary shrine within the grounds.
